questions.question: Market Based Economic Dispatch (MBED) Mechanism is related with which of the following ministry?

options.text: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Market Based Economic Dispatch (MBED) Mechanism** is an approach used in the power sector to optimize the **allocation of electricity generation resources.**
 
• It is implemented and overseen by the **Ministry of Power in many countries.**
 
• In traditional power systems, the dispatch of power plants was primarily determined by the system operator based on technical and operational considerations, such as system stability and reliability.
 
• However, with the increasing penetration of renewable energy sources and the liberalization of the electricity market, there is a need for a more economically efficient approach to dispatching power generation.
 
• **The MBED mechanism introduces market principles into the dispatch process, allowing the economic forces of supply and demand to determine the allocation of electricity generation resources.**
 
• It involves the establishment of electricity markets where power producers compete to sell their **electricity, and buyers (such as distribution companies and industrial consumers) compete to purchase the electricity.​**

**​** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** The Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA)** is a government ministry in India that is responsible for the administration and regulation of corporate affairs in the country.

 
 
• It is one of the key **ministries under the Government of India.**
 
• The primary objective of the Ministry of** Corporate Affairs is to ensure the proper functioning and regulation of the corporate sector in India. **
 
 
 
• **​The Ministry of Finance is a government ministry** that is responsible for the financial and economic matters of a country.
 
 
• Its primary objective is to formulate and implement fiscal policies, manage public finances, and ensure the stability and growth of the economy. 
 
 
 
• **The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) **is a **government ministry in India** that is responsible for the **promotion, development, and enhancement of competitiveness of micro, small, and medium enterprises.**
 
• It was established in **2007** with the aim of creating a conducive environment for the growth of these enterprises, which play a vital role in the Indian economy.

questions.question: Which of the following has been designated as the self-regulatory origination for** Micro finance **institutions in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sa-Dhan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Microfinance **refers to the **financial services provided **to **low-income individuals **or **groups **who are **typically **excluded from **traditional banking**.
 
• **Most microfinance institutions focus **on **offering credit **in the **form of small working capital loans**, sometimes called **microloans **or **microcredit**.
 
• **Sa-Dhan's mission **is to build the **field of community development finance **in India to help **its member and associate institutions **to better **serve low-income households**, **particularly women**, in **both rural **and **urban India**, in their **quest **for **establishing stable livelihoods and improving quality of life**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana **is a **financial inclusion program **of the **Government of India open **to **Indian citizens**, that aims to **expand affordable access **to **financial services **such **as bank accounts**, **remittances**, **credit**, **insurance, and pensions**.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are FALSE with respect to simple model of the circular flow of economy?

i. The aggregate consumption is more than the aggregate expenditure.

ii. There is government intervention.

iii. There are no trade activities with the rest of the world.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only i**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The basic circular flow model of the economy **operates without government intervention.
 
• This model illustrates the interconnected flow of money, goods, and services among economic participants.
 
• It serves as the foundation for national accounting and macroeconomics.
 
• Additional details about the **circular flow model** include:
 
 
• It delineates the overall structure of the economy, depicting exchanges between households and firms through both the factor and product markets.
 
• Households contribute land, labor, and capital to firms.
 
• Households purchase goods and services from firms in the product market.
 
• Firms compensate households for the resources they supply, which constitute factors of production.
 
• In reality, the model becomes more intricate with the inclusion of two additional elements: government involvement.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Various circular flow models exist, each tracking a different number of sectors. 
 
• The following sectors could be incorporated into a circular flow model. Typically, each sector is denoted by a capital letter, often associated with GDP calculation methods. 
 
• Governments determine their gross national income by monitoring all injections into and withdrawals from the circular flow of income. When leaks match injections, the circular flow of income for a nation is deemed balanced.

questions.question: In December 2017, SEBI raised the investment limit for FPIs in central government securities to over _______ from January 2018.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rs. 1.91 lakh crore.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In December 2017, SEBI raised the investment limit for FPIs in central government securities to over Rs. 1.91 lakh crore from January 2018, which was earlier Rs. 1,89,700 crore.
 
• This move has been made as a part of the effort by SEBI to push the inflow in the country’s capital markets from overseas investors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__****SEBI**

 
• SEBI stands for **Securities and Exchange Board of India.**
 
• The SEBI is the regulator of the **securities and commodity market in the country owned by the Indian Government**.
 
• SEBI was established on 12 April **1988** and its **headquarters** are located in **Mumbai**.
 
• The regional offices of SEBI are located in **Ahmadabad, Kolkata, Chennai, and Delhi.**
 
• On 30 January **1992**, Statutory powers were given to it through the **SEBI Act, 1992.**

questions.question: Which of these statements is true?

options.text: Under competitive asset market conditions, the price of a bond must always be equal to its present value in equilibrium.
Under competitive asset market conditions, the price of a bond must be less than its present value to benefit the seller.
Under competitive asset market conditions, the price of a bond must exceed its present value to benefit the buyer.
Under competitive asset market conditions, the present value must exceed the price of a bond to benefit the seller.

questions.solution: The correct answer is __**Under competitive asset market conditions, the price of a bond must always be equal to its present value in equilibrium.**__

questions.question: Which among the following is the correct way to express change of inventories of a firm during a year?

options.text: Change of inventories of a firm during a year (value added – intermediate goods used by the firm + sale of the firm during a year)
Change of inventories of a firm during a year (value added + intermediate goods used by the firm + sale of the firm during a year)
Change of inventories of a firm during a year (value added – intermediate goods used by the firm – sale of the firm during a year)
Change of inventories of a firm during a year (value added + intermediate goods used by the firm – sale of the firm during a year)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Change of inventories of a firm during a year (value added + intermediate goods used by the firm – sale of the firm during a year).**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Point__**

 
• The correct way to express the change of inventories of a firm during a year is by calculating the inventory turnover or by using the formula for the change in inventories.
 
 
• **Inventory Turnover:**

 
 
• Inventory turnover is a financial ratio that measures the number of times a company's inventory is sold and replaced during a given period.
 
• It is calculated by dividing the cost of goods sold (COGS) by the average inventory value.
 
• The formula for inventory turnover is:
 
 
• **Inventory Turnover = Cost of Goods Sold / Average Inventory**
 
 
 
 
 
• **Change in Inventories::-**
 
 
• The change in inventories can be calculated by subtracting the ending inventory value from the beginning inventory value.
 
• The formula for the change in inventories is:
 
 
• **Change in Inventories = Ending Inventory - Beginning Inventory**
 
• This measure represents the net increase or decrease in inventory over a specific period, such as a year. A positive value indicates an increase in inventory, while a negative value suggests a decrease.

questions.question: Which economic thought talks about methodological individualism, or the idea that people will act in meaningful ways which can be analysed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Austrian economic thought**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__ 

__
 
• **Austrian economic thought**

 
 
• Austrian economic thought talks about methodological **individualism** or the idea that people will act in meaningful ways which can be analyzed.
 
• The Austrian school uses the logic of a priori thinking—something a person can think on their own without relying on the outside world—to discover economic laws of universal application, whereas other mainstream schools of economics, like the neoclassical school, the new Keynesians, and others, make use of data and mathematical models to prove their point objectively.
 
• In this respect, the Austrian school can be more specifically **contrasted with the German historical school** that rejects the universal application of any economic theorem.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__ 

 
• **Keynesian Economics**

 
 
• **Keynesian economics is a macroeconomic economic theory of total spending in the economy and its effects on output, employment, and inflation.**
 
• Keynesian economics was developed by the British economist John Maynard Keynes during the 1930s in an attempt to understand the **Great Depression.**
 
• Keynesian economics is considered a "**demand-side**" theory that focuses on changes in the economy over the short run.
 
• Keynes’s theory was the first to sharply separate the study of economic behaviour and markets based on individual incentives from the study of broad national economic aggregate variables and constructs. 
 
 
 
• **Laissez-Faire**
 
 
• Laissez-faire is an economic theory from the 18th century that opposed any government intervention in business affairs.
 
• The driving principle behind laissez-faire, a French term that translates to "leave alone" (literally, "let you do"), is that the less the government is involved in the economy, the better off business will be, and by extension, society as a whole.
 
• **Laissez-faire economics is a key part of free-market capitalism.**

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a component of investment?

options.text: Money spent on purchasing shares of a company
Machinery and equipment employed by a firm
Inventories of raw materials stocked by a firm

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Money spent on purchasing shares of a company.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Investment is defined as the purchase of goods that are not consumed today but are used in the future to create wealth.**
 
• **In addition to residential construction, machinery and equipment employed by a firm, and inventories of raw materials stocked by a firm are all components of investment as they are used to generate future income.**
 
• Money spent on purchasing shares of a company is not a component of investment as it does not directly create wealth or generate future income.
 
• However, investing in shares can indirectly contribute to wealth creation through dividends and capital gains.
 
• It is important to note that investment can take various forms, including financial assets like stocks and bonds, as well as physical assets like real estate and machinery.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Addition to residential construction: **This is a component of investment as it involves spending money on building or improving a property, which can generate future income through rent or sale.
 
• **Machinery and equipment employed by a firm:** This is a component of investment as it involves spending money on tools and equipment that can increase productivity and generate future income for the firm.
 
• **Inventories of raw materials stocked by a firm:** This is a component of investment as it involves spending money on goods that can be used to produce finished products and generate future income for the firm.

questions.question: Spot the difference.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Intrinsic value**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Intrinsic value** is a concept that refers to the inherent, true value of an asset, independent of its market value.
 
• It's often used in investing to determine whether a stock is under or overvalued by comparing its intrinsic value to its current market price.
 
• The calculation of **intrinsic value** can involve fundamental analysis of the company's financial health, including earnings, dividends, and growth rates.
 
• Unlike other options such as a legal proposition, prescribed currency, or guarantee of issuing company, **intrinsic value** is a financial metric rather than a legal or currency-related term.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Investment Term
 Description
 
 
 
 

 Market Value
 The current price at which an asset or service can be bought or sold.
 
 

 Fundamental Analysis
 A method of measuring a security's intrinsic value by examining related economic and financial factors.
 
 

 Dividend
 A portion of a company's earnings distributed to shareholders.
 
 

 Growth Rate
 The amount by which a company's earnings are expected to grow, often used in intrinsic value calculations.
 
 

 Value Investing
 An investment strategy that involves picking stocks that appear to be trading for less than their intrinsic or book value.

questions.question: Sociologist Jan Breman described the change in the nature of the relationship between landlords, belonging to the dominant class, and agricultural workers, belonging to the low caste, as a shift from ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**patronage to exploitation.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• The shift from **patronage to exploitation** refers to a change in the relationship between** landlords and agricultural workers,** where landlords used to provide **support and protection** to workers but now exploit them for their labor.
 
• The rise in migrant agricultural labor was a result of the commercialization of agriculture.
 
• A **pattern of seasonal migration** developed, with thousands of workers moving between their **homes and more prosperous areas** where there is a demand for **labor and higher wages,** as traditional bonds between** laborers or tenants **and landlords broke down and as seasonal demand for agricultural laborers increased in prosperous areas.
 
• Workers also** leave rural areas** due to rising **inequality **that began in the mid-1990s and pushed many households to work several jobs in order to make ends meet.
 
• This change is significant because it reflects a shift in **power dynamics** between the **dominant class** and** low castes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tenant to tiller** does** not** reflect a change in the nature of the relationship between landlords and workers, but rather a change in the type of** labor arrangement.**

 
 
• Farmers, or land tillers, have the legal right to acquire** land ownership** under the "Land to Tiller" law.​
 
 
 
• **Exploitation to patronage** contradicts the description provided by Jan Breman and** does not** reflect a shift in power dynamics.
 
• **Bonded labor to free labor** refers to a specific type of l**abor arrangement **rather than a change in the nature of the relationship between landlords and workers.
